ai.title: Cap researcher-web steps at 15 and add thinker-gemini routing rules
ai.summary: The `researcher-web` agent now enforces a hard limit of 15 research steps via a new `handleSteps` generator, preventing runaway loops that previously consumed excessive compute. When the limit is reached without a final answer, the agent yields an `add_message` tool call to force a written response before terminating. Concurrently, the `base-chat` agent's instructions are updated to mandate spawning `thinker-gemini` for any reasoning, logic, or architecture tasks, replacing its previous default behavior of reasoning internally. A third change expands `docs/testing.md` with guidance on avoiding flaky tests that poll for intermediate states in async operations.
ai.evidence: In `agents/researcher/researcher-web.ts`, a new `handleSteps` generator is added that caps research steps at `MAX_RESEARCH_STEPS = 15` and forces a final answer via `add_message` when the researcher does not complete. In `agents/base-chat.ts`, the `instructionsPrompt` is updated to explicitly direct the use of the `thinker-gemini` agent for reasoning tasks and to skip it for trivial queries. In `docs/testing.md`, new paragraphs describe a flake pattern where polling samples the middle of async work and recommend using `EngineRegistry.backgroundSettled()`.
ai.unknowns: The specific text of the forced final answer message in `researcher-web.ts` is omitted in the diff, so the exact prompt given to the model at step 16 is not visible.

changes.what: Added a step budget of 15 to `researcher-web` and a forced final answer mechanism to prevent infinite research loops.
Updated `base-chat` instructions to delegate all non-trivial reasoning to the `thinker-gemini` agent.

eli5.text: The web research helper now stops after fifteen searches to prevent it from looping endlessly and wasting computing power, and the main chat assistant now sends complex thinking tasks to a dedicated helper instead of working through them on its own. This affects anyone using the free online chat assistant who asks questions requiring detailed analysis or research. You will notice the research process finishes more reliably, and complex problems get handed to a specialized thinking tool that takes full context into account before giving an answer.

ai.title: Peak-hours time-zone formatters now reject unsupported zone names
ai.summary: In `common/src/constants/freebuff-peak-hours.ts`, a new `isSupportedTimeZone` helper probes whether a runtime can construct a date-time formatter for a given zone, because unsupported names such as `Etc/Unknown` trigger a range error. The existing `resolveWindowTimeZone` function now runs that probe before returning a zone, so both explicit and runtime-reported values fall back to `FALLBACK_WINDOW_TIME_ZONE` when the engine rejects them. This prevents the web model picker from throwing during label render on devices whose internationalization data cannot read the local zone.
ai.evidence: The diff adds `isSupportedTimeZone` to `common/src/constants/freebuff-peak-hours.ts` and rewrites `resolveWindowTimeZone` to call it, falling back to `FALLBACK_WINDOW_TIME_ZONE` when the zone name is rejected by `Intl.DateTimeFormat` construction.

eli5.text: The assistant now checks whether your device can display local time labels before trying to use them; if it cannot, the interface falls back to a universal standard time zone instead of crashing. This protects people using web browsers on gaming consoles or certain desktop systems that cannot properly identify their own time zone. You will no longer see a blank or broken screen when the model picker loads; the times simply display in standard time.

facts: Bun's own crash report saying this CPU cannot run the optimized build.
CPU: sse42 avx Features: no_avx2 panic: Illegal instruction at address 0x7FF61902F82C panicked during a panic. Aborting.

Three spellings of one failure, at two levels of certainty. SIGILL STATUS_ILLEGAL_INSTRUCTION, or Bun's crash report naming the missing feature (see stderrReportsMissingCpuFeature), is proof this CPU cannot run this build; a Windows startup abort is a strong suspicion (see isStartupCpuFeatureCrash).

Any failed exit, not only a native crash code: a Bun crash on Windows usually exits with plain code 3, and the reason is only in its stderr (see stderrReportsMissingCpuFeature). Clean exits skip the wait.
entries.title: CLI update: launcher
entries.summary: CLI changes across 1 file(s) (+254/−11).

ai.title: Launcher detects Bun AVX2 crash via stderr on Windows code 3
ai.summary:
The Freebuff launcher now reads Bun's stderr tail and matches it against two new constants, BUN_NO_AVX2_FEATURE (/^Features:[^
]*\bno_avx2\b/m) and BUN_ILLEGAL_INSTRUCTION_PANIC (/^panic(?:\([^)\n]*\))?: Illegal instruction at address 0x[0-9a-f]+/im), to confirm a missing AVX2 instruction set. Previously the Windows baseline fallback only fired on STATUS_ILLEGAL_INSTRUCTION (0xC000001D) or the startup abort 0xC0000409, but a Bun native crash on a pre-AVX2 CPU exits with plain code 3 and the reason is only visible in its stderr. tryFallbackToBaseline() now treats stderrReportsMissingCpuFeature as a confirmed illegal-instruction event and records the machine as lacking AVX2 before downloading the baseline binary, while ordinary exit 3 passes through untouched.
ai.evidence: In cli/release-core/launcher.js, stderrReportsMissingCpuFeature() tests Bun's stderr tail against BUN_NO_AVX2_FEATURE and BUN_ILLEGAL_INSTRUCTION_PANIC regexes, and attachExitHandler() now captures stderrTail for any non-zero exit (code !== 0 || signal) instead of only Windows native crash codes, feeding it to tryFallbackToBaseline().
ai.migration: Freebuff, Codebuff, and Codecane users on pre-AVX2 Windows CPUs no longer hit a crash-loop on the optimized build and are automatically moved to the baseline binary on the next launch.
